title: Chicken Thighs With Brussels Sprouts & Butternut Squash on a Sheet Pan
description: By Food & Wine’s Julia Levy: When it comes to weeknight dinners, sheet pan recipes are the ultimate kitchen heroes: minimal prep, easy cleanup, and maximum flavor payoff. This maple-miso chicken with brussels sprouts and butternut squash checks all those boxes and more. The recipe layers savory white miso and soy sauce with the warming bite of fresh ginger and garlic, then balances that intensity with pure maple syrup. The result is chicken thighs that roast up golden-brown and deeply flavorful.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (about a ¾-inch piece)
1 1/2 teaspoons lower-sodium soy sauce or tamari
6 tablespoons neutral oil (such as avocado or canola), divided
6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 2 pounds total)
1 small (1 1/2 pound) butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and cut into 1-inch pieces (about 4 cups)
1 pound brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved lengthwise (left whole if small) (about 4 cups)
3 cups loosely packed baby arugula (3 ounces)
directions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Finely chop white and light green parts of scallions and place in a large bowl; set aside. Thinly slice dark green parts of scallions and set aside. Add miso, maple syrup, ginger, soy sauce, garlic, and 4 tablespoons oil to chopped scallions in large bowl; whisk together until mostly smooth. Reserve 1/4 cup miso mixture in a small bowl, and set aside.

Add chicken thighs to miso mixture in large bowl, and add 1/4 teaspoon each salt and pepper; rub chicken thighs with mixture until evenly coated. Let stand, uncovered, at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Toss together squash, brussels sprouts, remaining 2 tablespoons oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper on a large rimmed baking sheet; spread in an even layer. Top with marinated chicken thighs. Bake the chicken until a thermometer inserted into thickest portion of thighs registers 165°F and vegetables are tender and browned, 40 to 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk vinegar and toasted sesame oil into reserved 1/4 cup miso mixture in small bowl until smooth and emulsified; set dressing aside.

Transfer chicken to a plate. Add arugula and reserved sliced scallions to baking sheet with vegetables; toss with reserved dressing until evenly coated. Return chicken to baking sheet; garnish with sesame seeds, and serve immediately.
